reasoning: Satellite records of Arctic sea ice extent began in 1979. According to authoritative scientific organizations including NOAA, the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC), and the European Environment Agency (EEA), Arctic sea ice has shown a steep, statistically significant decline since satellite observations began. Specifically, summer minimum sea ice extent has decreased by about 13% per decade, with total September sea ice coverage having roughly halved between 1979 and recent years.
